packageRules.description: Expo SDK is a coupled bundle (bundledNativeModules.json). Bump via a single SDK-upgrade story, not per-package — see epics.md Maintenance section M1.

Tamagui is a coupled compiler/runtime bundle across @tamagui/core, @tamagui/web, @tamagui/animations-*, @tamagui/babel-plugin, @tamagui/next-plugin, and the tamagui umbrella. Per-package bumps fragment the ecosystem (closed PR #34). Bump via a single Tamagui-upgrade story — see epics.md Maintenance section M2.

React (+ react-dom + @types/react + @types/react-dom) is pinned by Expo SDK 54's bundledNativeModules.json to an exact version. Bumping the `react19` catalog out of band crosses the SDK contract — closed PR #37 demonstrated this when dependabot tried 19.1.4 → 19.2.6. Bump via the M1 Expo SDK upgrade story, not per-package.

ESLint core + @eslint/js have a peer-dep matrix that breaks at install if either is bumped alone. Closed PRs #39 (@eslint/js 9→10) and #40 (eslint 9→10) both demonstrated the trap. Bump as one coordinated story alongside eslint-plugin-* peer-range audits — see epics.md Maintenance section M3. typescript-eslint and other plugins whose peer range explicitly accepts v9 + v10 are NOT ignored — they can land independently.

@types/node major must match the Node runtime engines pin (package.json `engines.node: ^22.21.0`). Bumping types ahead of runtime lets code compile against APIs the runtime doesn't have — tsc can't catch this. Closed PR #45 demonstrated: dependabot tried catalog ^22.18.12 → ^25.9.1 while engines stayed at ^22. Patches/minors within the same major are still welcome (security fixes).
